newsitem.title: UK: British schools hit by discipline crisis.
newsitem.headline: British schools hit by discipline crisis.

text.p: British classrooms, once regarded as a bastion of order, are now under the spotlight over a crisis in discipline which has raised a national debate about standards of morality.

The focus centred on the Ridings School in Halifax, northern England, which was closed by local authorities on Thursday after its teachers voted overwhelmingly to strike in protest at attacks by children whom they said were unteachable.
Unions for the embattled teachers said a woman teacher was sexually assaulted while a male teacher was punched in the face. Authorities said the school would reopen next week with a new head teacher.
But education has become an emotionally-charged battlefield for politicians vying for the support they need to win the next general election, due by next May.

Politicians competing for the moral high ground are putting every outburst of classroom anarchy under the microscope. They and the media play up fears that social values are breaking down in once-tranquil Britain.

Right-wingers want caning brought back in schools and Frances Lawrence, widow of a London headmaster stabbed to death by a teenager, struck a chord with Britons when she urged a new morality code in a country hit by rising violence.
An opinion poll in The London Times on Friday showed that Britons were now more worried about crime than unemployment.
Twice as many people thought the opposition Labour Party was more likely than the ruling Conservatives to tackle violence and promote good citizenship along the lines put forward by Lawrence.
Education Secretary Gillian Shephard, at the eye of the classroom storm, was publicly rebuked this week by Prime Minister John Major when she supported a return to caning, banned in Britain in 1985.

Major, whose own "back to basics" morality campaign badly misfired after several leading Conservatives became mired in sex or corruption scandals, said the government had no intention of bringing back corporal punishment.
Morality is now headline news in a country where many politicians, parents and teachers fear they have lost their self-confidence and sense of moral direction to combat lawlessness.

New legislation will ban virtually all handguns after 16 young Scottish children and their teacher were killed by a lone gunman in Dublane early this year and pressure is building for cross-party consensus on banning all combat knives.
